rows.courseDescription: This course explores how organizations use predictive AI to make repeatable, data-informed decisions at scale and extract value from generative AI. Students learn to build and evaluate models using historical business data and translate predictions into actions, personalized experiences, and resource allocation. The course examines how predictive and generative AI complement one another: generative AI extracts information and creates new content and alternatives, while predictive AI estimates outcomes and guides which options to use, for whom, and under what conditions. Applications span customer management, marketing, pricing, forecasting, and operational planning, with examples including personalized targeting, content selection, and adaptive experimentation. Through lectures, business cases, vibe coding, and a team project, students develop practical skills in building AI solutions that connect data and models to measurable business outcomes.

The application for the Spring 2027 offering of Renewable Energy Project Finance (MGT 683) is TBA. Upon enrollment in MGT 683, students will have 50 points deducted from their course auction balance. We anticipate that student interest will exceed the number of available slots for the course. If you are not allocated a slot initially, your name will be placed on a waiting list, and you will be informed if additional space clears, up to one week prior to the start of the semester. This course is cross-listed with ENV 635 and follows the Yale School of the Environment academic calendar. 
The course is intended to be a practicum, exposing students to real-world tools of the trade as well as the theory underlying them. In place of a textbook, students will read approximately 400 pages of legal contracts and engineering reports from a U.S. renewable energy project. Through weekly homework assignments, students develop the skills necessary to construct a detailed financial model, largely comparable to what would be used by an investment firm, project developer, or independent power producer. Modeling skills include sizing debt capacity, sensitivity analysis, stochastic forecasting, taxes, and 3-way financial statements. Lectures introduce energy market dynamics, financial structuring, equipment engineering, risk management, and alternative contractual frameworks. While the primary lecturer will teach on Zoom for as much as three weeks per month, students are expected to attend all lectures in person, where members of the teaching team will be physically present to coordinate discussion and Q&A.
